subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — commit bands, discounting, and throughput test protocol
messages:
From: Sara Morales <sara.morales@omnihealth.com>

Cc: Tom Liang <tliang@omnihealth.com>, procurement@omnihealth.com

Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry and measurement expectations

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our engineering leads want clarity on three things before we progress: 1) how you size a GPU pool for a committed baseline, 2) the tokens/sec and requests/sec guarantees you can offer per commit band, and 3) the exact measurement protocol you'll use to validate throughput & latency during acceptance.

We shared a short commit request PDF (attached) that shows our expected 95th-percentile latency goals for a 256-token average completion and a throughput target of ~1.2M tokens/day. We are price-sensitive and will need a discount schedule tied to annual commit bands. Can you propose a pricing structure + an acceptance test plan we can sign off on?

- Sara
Senior Product Manager, OmniHealth
Attachment: Omni_Commit_Request_v1.pdf
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Sara Morales <sara.morales@omnihealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-19T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry and measurement expectations

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. High level reply below; I also attached a concise test plan spreadsheet.

Summary proposal (first pass):
- Commit bands (annual pre-pay):
  - Band A: 20k GPU-hours/year — baseline (no discount)
  - Band B: 60k GPU-hours/year — 18% discount
  - Band C: 120k GPU-hours/year — 30% discount + 1 week burst capacity per quarter
- Baseline throughput guarantees (per committed pool):
  - Tokens/sec: we guarantee a sustained steady-state of X tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU; we’ll map to your expected token mix during sizing.
  - Requests/sec: guarantees depend on request size; for 256-token average completions we target N reqs/sec for each GPU equivalent (see sheet).
- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 220ms for 256-token completions on warm cache, measured during steady-state.

Measurement/acceptance outline (short):
1) Test harness: we run your real prompt set (or a validated synthetic seed set) through our load driver (k6/Locust).
2) Warm-up: 10-minute warm-up with KV cache population and normal concurrency to reach steady-state.
3) Steady-state run: 20-minute test window; collect token throughput, req/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, and p50/p95/p99 latencies.
4) Cold-start run: 5x cold start samples (instances cycled) to measure tail behavior.
5) Pass criteria: tokens/sec and requests/sec within 95% of target and p95 latency <= committed target in at least 4/5 steady-state windows.

I'll follow up with a more numeric mapping (tokens/sec per A100e) after Marcus confirms hardware assumptions. Attaching: throughput-test-plan.xlsx (draft).

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: throughput-test-plan.xlsx

Priyom — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions from our infra/bench team:
- Can you provide concrete numbers (tokens/sec and req/sec) we can expect per GPU rather than the X/N placeholders?
- How do you adjust guarantees if our average prompt length moves from 256 to 512 tokens?
- For the pass criteria, can we require both warm-cache and cold-start windows to pass (not OR)? We've had regressions where steady-state looked fine but cold-starts blew p95.

Also, on discounting: our procurement lead wants a structured table that ties discount % directly to committed GPU-hours and an SLA credit schedule if throughput/latency misses occur. Can you produce that as a formal appendix we can review?

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Infrastructure, OmniHealth
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Tom Liang <tliang@omnihealth.com>, Sara Morales <sara.morales@omnihealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-19T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry and measurement expectations

Tom — great questions. Below I pin concrete numbers and an adjusted acceptance rule that addresses cold-start concerns. Marcus also chimed in on hardware sizing and quantization knobs.

Concrete mapping (example configuration we typically size on):
- Unit = 1 A100-80GB equivalent (A100e) with FF32/AMP optimizations and LLM kernel set.
- 1 A100e sustained (warm) throughput: ~3800 tokens/sec for a 256-token avg completion workload at N=1 beam, typical open model (your model may vary +/- 15%).
- Requests/sec (256-token avg): ~14 reqs/sec per A100e (sustained, steady-state).
- For 512-token avg: tokens/sec per GPU similar but req/sec roughly halves (so ~7 reqs/sec), and p95 latency expectation increases by ~1.8x in heavy utilization scenarios.

Sizing example for your 1.2M tokens/day target:
- 1.2M tokens/day => ~13.9 tokens/sec sustained (24/7). With steady-state overheads and expected peak bursts, we'd recommend a 4x headroom factor during sizing => target pool: 56 tokens/sec effective capacity => ~0.015 A100e (practically, we'd provision a small fleet: 1-2 A100e depending on burst and redundancy needs). For production-grade multi-tenant isolation and predictable burst, we commonly recommend starting at 4 A100e for high-availability, then adjust after an acceptance run.

Updated acceptance rule (requested):
- Both warm-cache and cold-start windows must meet pass thresholds. Warm: 4/5 steady-state windows pass. Cold: 3/4 cold-start windows pass. If either fails, we iterate (tuning quantization, batch sizes) and re-run once for free as part of initial onboarding.

Discount + SLA appendix (summary):
- Band A (20k GPU-hrs/yr): base price, SLA: 98.5% uptime, throughput/latency credits start at 5% service credit for single-metric miss.
- Band B (60k GPU-hrs/yr): 18% off list, SLA: 99.0% uptime, credits escalate to 10% for sustained misses (>72 hours).
- Band C (120k GPU-hrs/yr): 30% off list, 99.5% uptime, punitive credits + prioritized on-call support and quarterly architectural review.

Marcus: can you confirm the A100e numeric baseline above (tokens/sec / reqs/sec) and add any quantization/parallelization notes?

- Priyom

On Thu, Nov 19, 2026 at 11:18 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Confirming the baseline numbers — they are derived from our A100-optimized kernel build and represent median performance across 20 models we benchmarked. Quantization (4-bit) reduces memory pressure and can increase tokens/sec by ~12% in inference-bound workloads but will need quality checks. Also recommend enabling prefix caching for chat-style workloads to reduce head-room needs.
>
> - Marcus
